sludge from anaerobic swinelagoons of different types of swine operation and from different swine companies had similar N availability and that 41% of the N in sludge was in a plant available form.
the availability of N from sludge of different companies and different types of swine production operations was the same.

sludge from different swine companies and different types of swine operation (i.e. sow, nursery, and finishing) had no significant effects on the availability of nitrogen (i.e. inorganic and organic N) in sludge from lagoons associated with those operations.

the availability of N from swine sludge.
the potential of swine sludge as a source of N for crop production.
the availability of N from sludge from anaerobic swill lagoons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sludge N availability is not significantly affected by the company or the type of swine production system from which the sludge was obtained, but that this statement needs to be tested in the field before being applied in a general manner.
sludge N mineralized in the 12 weeks of incubation was similar regardless of sludge source.
sludge from anaerobic swill waste treatment lagoans from different types of operations can be applied to the same crop without concern of different N availabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sludge from anaerobic lagoons of different swine operations can be considered to be of equal N availability for crop use.
sludge N availability from different swine companies and types of operations can be assumed to be similar, and thus a single N availability coefficient can be used for all sludge sources.
, regardless of source, sludge from lagoons has a high plant N availability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sludge from anaerobic swines lagoons has a significant amount of N in plant available form.
sludge from different swine companies and different swine operations can be used interchangeably for N fertilization of crops.
the N availability of swine sludge can be reliably predicted by the sludge source, regardless of the type of swine operations and companies.
